 W.P.(C).Nos.39634 of 2016 & 25257 of 2017  ------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 23rd day of August, 2017

J U D G M E N T I am considering these two writ petitions together because they have been filed by the same petitioner, involving similar circumstances and the reliefs in one would depend upon the relief to be granted in the other.

For the sake of convenience, I treat W.P.(C). No.39634 of 2016 as the leading case and all reference to parties and documents in this judgment will be, unless otherwise specifically stated, as shown in the said writ petition.

2. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner in both writ petitions Sri.Anilkumar M.Sivaraman; the learned Standing Counsel Sri.Thomas Abraham, appearing for the 3rd respondent and the learned Senior Government Pleader appearing on behalf of respondents 1and 2.
3.

The petitioner is stated to be an unregistered association of women, who calls themselves the 'Annapoorna Vanitha Canteen', which they say is a unit of the Kudumbasree CDS attached to the Nedumangad Municipality.

According to them, they were running a canteen in the Nedumangad Taluk District Hospital, which is now called the District Hospital, for the last more than 18 years and their complaint is that their services were terminated by the Superintendent of the said Hospital, the 1st respondent herein, W.P.(C).Nos.39634 of 2016 & 25257 of 2017 without notice to them and therefore, that it is illegal.
They, on such allegation, pray in W.P.(C).No.39634 of 2016 that they be permitted by the 1st respondent to run the canteen without interruption.

As regards W.P.(C).No.25257 of 2017 is concerned, the claim of the petitioner is that an amount of 3,71,000/- is due to them from the Hospital and they pray that this amount be returned to them by the Annapoornavanitha Canteen vs The Superintendent on 6 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14406999/
3 respondents, without delay.
4. The pleadings on record would show that the petitioner's assertion is that they have been running a canteen in the Hospital for the last more than 18 years.

However, the petitioner has not been able to present on record any document to show how they were allowed to operate this canteen uninterruptedly and without specific contracts being entered into for the last 18 years.

I can only visualise such situation because it being a Kudumbasree Unit, the petitioner was allowed to run the canteen of the Hospital without a proper tender and without calling for other competitors for the several years past.
This, in my view, cannot give the petitioner a vested right to maintain that they should be allowed to run the canteen for all years to come.
I am certain that the running of the canteen, being one run in the public domain, will have to be controlled and regulated by the competent Authorities in terms of law.

It will certainly be required that a tender is floated and competitors invited for the purpose of running the canteen on an W.P.(C).Nos.39634 of 2016 &
25257 of 2017 year to year basis.
In this case, this has not been done in the past.

5. I also notice that it is the specific case of the 1st respondent that subsequent to the decision taken to terminate the services of the petitioner, they had published a tender notification on 08.11.2016 and that more than 22 persons participated in the said tender which was then granted in favour a lady called Ms.Aswathy for an amount of 77,000/-.

According to the 1st respondent, the petitioner was only paying 3,000/- per month and therefore, that the grant of tender in favour the aforementioned Ms.Aswathy for an amount of 77,000/-, has obtained to the Hospital a profit of 74,000/- per month.
I am certain that this is a factor which is clearly against the contentions of the petitioner.

The petitioner cannot maintain that they should be allowed to run the canteen without a tender and that, no competitors can be allowed because they have been operating for the last 18 years without interruption.

In such view of the matter, the contention of the petitioner that they should be allowed to run the canteen for ever does not appeal to me and I, therefore, have to repel such contentions.
6.

As regards the claim of the petitioner, in W.P.(C).No.25257 of 2017, that an amount of 3,71,000/-
is due to them is concerned, I see that this claim is based on Ext.P1 statement of account made by the them before the 1st respondent under the "Mother and Child Free Food Scheme".

entities.text: Mother and Child Free Food Scheme
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner submits W.P.(C).Nos.39634 of 2016 & 25257 of 2017 that the claim of the petitioner has, in fact, been admitted by the 1st respondent, as is evidenced by Ext.P4 information obtained by them.
However, the learned Senior Government Pleader submits that in Ext.P4 there is no admission as to the amounts due to the petitioner.
All what is stated therein is that some amounts have not been paid but that the quantification of such amounts have not been yet done.

This Court would not be in a position, while acting under the mandate of Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to decide the entitlement or the quantum of amount due to the petitioner based on Ext.P1, since it requires an evaluation of factual circumstances and factors.
I am certainly of the view that this should be thus left to the competent Authority to consider and take a decision thereon.

7. In such circumstances and for the reasons that I have stated above, I dismiss W.P.(C).No.39634 of 2016 and order W.P.(C). No.25257 of 2017 directing the 1st respondent to consider the claim of the Annapoornavanitha Canteen vs The Superintendent on 6 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14406999/
4 petitioner for the amounts claimed by them under Ext.P1 statement of account, after affording an opportunity of being heard to the representative of the petitioner as expeditiously as possible, but not later than two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
8. I clarify that nothing contained in this judgment will be used against the petitioner, if they choose to respond to the notification calling for tenders to run the canteen for the next year and their W.P.(C).Nos.39634 of 2016 & 25257 of 2017 entitlement will be evaluated by the competent Authorities without being influenced or trammeled by anything contained in these two writ petitions and the proceedings before this Court.
These writ petitions are thus disposed of.

Sd/-
DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN, JUDGE.
